tldr: Uniform original-record multiplier calibration holds for fitted Gaussian counterfactual Stein discrepancy when only the intervention marginal is Gaussian. The broad calibration class imposes no conditional treated-density positivity, smoothness or moment envelope: its Gaussian mixture forces the required domination, feature moments and finite-rank tails. The theorem derives the projected Hilbert expansion, same-sample trace-norm covariance consistency, conditional distribution approximation and asymptotically exact rejection level, retaining heterogeneous treated strata, unknown mass, endpoint propensities and arbitrary controls. In the explicitly narrower positive \(C^1\) treated-density class with an eighth-moment envelope, legal local power includes the mass derivative and uses the central baseline critical value. The bounded legal tangent kernel is zero exactly when its signed intervention-density derivative vanishes. The sine-tilt family gives an exact covariance witness and a positive distributional gap supporting the need for original-record calibration.
gap: Fitted causal parameter inference does not calibrate the minimized counterfactual discrepancy. Direct-iid composite calibration concerns a different observation law. The missing result is a uniform primitive calibration theorem under a Gaussian restriction imposed only on the intervention marginal, allowing heterogeneous treated strata and same-sample nuisance estimation.
fill: The lead theorem derives the original-record projected limit and a consistent centered multiplier law uniformly over the interior marginal null. An explicit open family with fixed intervention marginal, assignment table and controls proves structural non-representability of the null law by those quantities. Only treated densities require positivity, continuous differentiability and a moment envelope. Fixed alternatives, local power, total computation and the legal-tangent open question give the inference result its practical scope.
